edited_fraction: median 252 (Astra) and 27 (Opus) changed weights per edit process, almost always in the final classification layer
cost_reported: median edit process about 3 min for Astra and Opus; open-weight editors used about 750 million prompt tokens; no comparison with baseline cost
evidence_notes: LLM editors working through the WeightLab tool server (read_weights, probe_*, set_weights, add_to_weights...; p.3, Table p.12) are the core of the study, with ERT as a training method to support them, so not peripheral; mechanism code_or_tensor_tool with probe feedback (closed loop). Open-weight results are mixed: DeepSeek 'matches the main editors on many of the completed cells' while GLM and Gemma are much weaker (p.6), so not coded as a clear failure; total network sizes are not given (largest head 61,470 parameters, p.3). Scripted closed-form editors were used only for tuning and baseline screens on ResNet-18, not on the agents' requests (p.8, Table 5), so non_llm_baseline is unclear; no preregistration, and release is promised, not done (p.1, Sec. H).
